table.notes: E11 baseline reproduced: no index at all, brute-force dot product over the full corpus.
hnswlib, M=16, ef_construction=200, ef=64, top-100. bytes/doc = 768 (float16 vectors) + 149.0 (HNSW graph, measured from a serialised index).
hnswlib, M=16, ef_construction=200, ef=128, top-100. bytes/doc = 768 (float16 vectors) + 149.0 (HNSW graph, measured from a serialised index).

Per-dimension symmetric int8 scalar quantisation (scale = max|value| / 127), dequantised on the fly for scoring; query stays float32. bytes/doc = 384 (int8 vectors) + 149.0 (graph) + 0.30 (per-dim scales, amortised). vs the float16 HNSW at the same ef=128: nDCG@10 0.7127 -> 0.7119 (-0.0008), recall@100 0.9450 -> 0.9417 (-0.0033).
E11 baseline reproduced: no index at all, exact MaxSim over every token of every document.

k-means k=4096 (2^12) fit on a 200,000-token subsample (MiniBatchKMeans); every token: 2-byte centroid id + 2-bit/dim residual against a 4-value shared scalar codebook (quantile buckets, ColBERTv2-style, not per-dim). Reconstructed and exact-MaxSim'd over the whole corpus per query - isolates storage cost, not retrieval latency (latency is close to the exhaustive f16 baseline by design).

k-means k=4096 (2^12) fit on a 200,000-token subsample (MiniBatchKMeans); every token: 2-byte centroid id + 1-bit/dim residual against a 2-value shared scalar codebook (quantile buckets, ColBERTv2-style, not per-dim). Reconstructed and exact-MaxSim'd over the whole corpus per query - isolates storage cost, not retrieval latency (latency is close to the exhaustive f16 baseline by design).

pylate.indexes.PLAID, fast-plaid backend, unmodified defaults (nbits=4 product-quantised residuals, n_ivf_probe=8, n_full_scores=8192); top-100 per query. Its returned score is PLAID's own centroid-pruned candidate generation reranked internally with reconstructed residual vectors. bytes/doc measured directly from the serialised index on disk (145,543,659 bytes total).
k_sim=4 (B=16 buckets), d_proj=16, R_reps=20 -> dim=5120. Exhaustive inner product over all 5183 docs' FDEs, top-100 taken as the final answer (no MaxSim rerank). bytes/doc is the FDE alone.

Same FDE (dim=5120) retrieval, top-100 reranked with exact MaxSim over the original float16 token vectors. bytes/doc therefore adds the full per-token float16 store (45245 B/doc) on top of the FDE - reranking needs the original vectors available for every document, not just the FDE.

FDE (dim=5120) placed in the same hnswlib index as the single-vector HNSW config (M=16, ef_construction=200, ef=128), top-100, then exact-MaxSim rerank over original float16 token vectors. bytes/doc adds the FDE (with its own measured graph overhead) and the full per-token float16 store needed for reranking.
k_sim=5 (B=32 buckets), d_proj=32, R_reps=20 -> dim=20480. Exhaustive inner product over all 5183 docs' FDEs, top-100 taken as the final answer (no MaxSim rerank). bytes/doc is the FDE alone.

Same FDE (dim=20480) retrieval, top-100 reranked with exact MaxSim over the original float16 token vectors. bytes/doc therefore adds the full per-token float16 store (45245 B/doc) on top of the FDE - reranking needs the original vectors available for every document, not just the FDE.
